title: Find a column narrows the Tech View Columns menu without changing ticks
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has it).
  2. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  3. In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.
  4. At least 1 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Esther Howard") and an email.
    • Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.
  5. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
  6. Create the work order: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it, and write down its number (e.g. "S1-702").
  7. On the work order page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard".
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab.
  3. Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
  4. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (in the design its tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
  5. Write down every column heading in Esther Howard's group.
  6. Click the Columns button in the toolbar (in the design its tooltip reads "Columns").
  7. Write down the count beside the menu heading (e.g. "10 of 10 shown") and every column listed with its tick.
  8. Click the menu's search box (in the design it reads "Find a column") and type ass
  9. Clear the box and type ASS (all capitals).
  10. Clear the box and type zzqx
  11. Clear the box.
  12. Close the Columns menu by clicking outside it.
  13. In the display switcher, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  14. Click Fields to display in the toolbar (the same place as Columns in Tech View).
  15. Type zzqx in its search box, then clear the box.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 8: only the columns whose name contains "ass" stay listed (e.g. "Asset" and "Assigned Techs"). The other columns disappear from the menu but keep their ticks.
  • Step 9: capitals give the same list. Upper or lower case does not matter.
  • Step 10: no column is listed and the menu says nothing matches (in the design: "No columns match"). Write down the words you see; a different wording alone is not a fail.
  • Steps 8 to 10: typing never ticks or unticks anything. The count from step 7 and the column headings from step 5 stay exactly the same.
  • Step 11: clearing the box brings back every column from step 7, each with the same tick.
  • Steps 14 and 15: Fields to display works the same way as the Columns menu: its search box narrows the field list by name, a search that finds nothing says so, and clearing it brings every field back with the same ticks. If Board View has no Fields to display button, mark the case Failed and write "no Fields to display picker" in the comment (the design has none; this is a known difference).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10048 (Story 5, Fields to display (Board View) and columns (Tech View)); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S2-R4, S5-R2, read 8 Oct 2026. Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Branko Cicovic, Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html) renders the Columns menu through the design system bundle _ds/shopview-design-system-fac6efcf…/_ds_bundle.js: search box "Find a column" (line 552), the menu keeps the columns whose name contains the typed text in any letter case (line 556), no-match text "No columns match" (line 580); ticks are kept separately from the search. Design crawl 8 Oct 2026: Tech View state 123 (Columns > Find a column, typed "Fib" and "zzqx-no-match": "10 of 10 shown | No columns match"). The search box and its wording are design-only details cited to the design; that Board View's Fields to display behaves the same way comes from S5-R2. Board View's missing Fields to display picker in the design is already recorded as a design-vs-spec difference. Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R4: “Tech View offers the same columns as List, plus the Assigned Techs column (Story 7), through its own column chooser (Story 5).”
  • S5-R2: “Board View offers a separate Fields to display picker in the same toolbar position and with the same interaction as the column chooser.”
